title: SRE Response Playbook: Rotations, Runbooks, Postmortems & Game Days
author: Maya R. Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operational response for production incidents: on-call rotation rules, primary runbook patterns, postmortem requirements, game day guidance, and status / customer-communication templates. Use this as the canonical reference for SREs, platform engineers, and on-call responders.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: All production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, inference runtime).
- Audience: SREs, platform engineers, incident commanders (ICs), triage engineers, support engineering, and engineering managers.

Key contacts and channels
-------------------------
- PagerDuty services:
  - Redwood - Serving (pd-service: redwood-serving-pd)
  - Redwood - Control Plane (pd-service: redwood-controlplane-pd)
  - Redwood - Networking (pd-service: redwood-net-pd)
- Slack channels:
  - #sre-oncall (primary incident comms)
  - #infra-ops (secondary escalation)
  - #eng-announce (for broad service-impact notices)
- Email alias for external-facing comms: status@redwood.ai

SLOs and critical thresholds (examples)
-------------------------------------
- redwood-api-gateway: P95 latency < 150ms, error rate < 0.5% per 5m.
- redwood-serving (generation): P95 time-to-first-token < 220ms, tail latency (99th) < 2.0s.
- embeddings-service: 99.9% availability monthly.

Alert severity and initial responder actions
------------------------------------------
- Sev 1 (P0) — outage impacting > 30% of traffic or critical loss of inference: immediate PD page to primary on-call. Escalation timeline: 2 min (phone), 5 min (SMS), 10 min (manager).
  1) Acknowledge the page within 2 minutes.
  2) Join incident bridge: https://meet.redwood.ai/incident (IC will create private conference on start).
  3) Post initial status to #sre-oncall and tag @oncall-lead.
  4) Execute the relevant runbook (see Runbook catalogue).
- Sev 2 (P1) — degraded performance or partial outage: PD to primary, respond within 15 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P2) — non-urgent bugs and single-customer issues: triage during business hours, PD to secondary only if escalation needed.

Escalation matrix
-----------------
- Primary -> Secondary -> Engineering Manager -> Platform Lead -> CTO (if > 4 hours unresolved for Sev 1).
- Example contacts:
  - Primary on-call: pd: redwood-serving-pd -> contact via PD; Slack: @primary_oncall.
  - Secondary on-call: pd: redwood-serving-pd-backup.
  - Platform escalations: @platform-lead on Slack.

Incident commander (IC) protocol
--------------------------------
1) Confirm incident and classify severity.
2) Set communication cadence (every 15m for P0/P1, hourly for P2).
3) Assign roles: Scribe, Communications lead, Mitigation lead, Postmortem lead.
4) Track actions in the incident doc (create Google doc using template link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-doc-template).
5) When mitigated, ensure customer-facing status update is issued and postmortem is assigned.

Runbook pattern (standardized)
-------------------------------
Every service runbook should follow this structure. Runbooks live in the Runbooks directory and are referenced from alert payloads.

- Title: Service name + runbook (e.g., redwood-serving - cold-start-high-latency)
- Pager triggers: alert IDs and severity mapping.
- Impact: short description of visible user impact.
- Quick checklist (immediate actions): 5 bullet checklist with commands.
- Diagnostics: key dashboards, queries, and commands.
- Mitigation steps (ordered): step-by-step reversible actions.
- Post-incident steps: metrics to collect, log pulls, and handoffs.
- Owner and last review date.

Sample runbook excerpt: redwood-serving - high-tail-latency
---------------------------------------------------------
Impact: Customers see increased token latency for >10% of requests, generation stalls observed.
Quick checklist:
1) Acknowledge alert in PD.
2) Check autoscaler and GPU pool health: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=redwood-serving
3) Verify example request path on canary node: curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' 
4) Check worker metrics dashboard: Grafana -> Serving / Tail latency (last 15m)

Diagnostics (commands) - run in sequence:
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep redwood-serving
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c inference-runtime --since=15m | grep -E "error|timeout"
- curl -sS "https://metrics-api.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"

Mitigation steps:
1) If autoscaler failing: restart HPA controller: kubectl rollout restart deployment/hpa-controller -n infra
2) If single node noisy: cordon + drain then redeploy: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
3) If kernel OOM and memory pressure: scale down batch size on model variant (see config: /configs/quantization-profiles/low-memory.json)

Post-incident tasks:
- Collect logs for 1 hour before/after remediation.
- Export traces for 99th percentile requests.
- Create postmortem doc within 72 hours.

On-call rotation rules
----------------------
- Rotation length: 7 days (Mon 00:00 UTC -> Sun 23:59 UTC).
- Shift handover window: 30 minutes overlap; outgoing on-call must provide a 15 minute summary in #sre-oncall.
- Primary and secondary assigned; primary handles PD pages, secondary handles edge escalations and backups.
- Time-off and coverage: swap requests must be recorded in the oncall calendar and a note posted to #sre-oncall at least 24 hours prior.
- Follow-the-sun: North America and Europe teams coordinate swaps during holidays; APAC coverage is arranged by request.

Game day program (quarterly)
----------------------------
Purpose: Validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, and surface gaps in tooling and observability.
Planning checklist (6 weeks out):
- Define scope (which service(s) to simulate).
- Book participants: SREs, product engineer(s), support, and security if required.
- Prepare injectable failure (e.g., node reboot, API rate limiter misconfiguration).
- Create a game day doc with objectives and success criteria.

During the exercise:
- Time-box the scenario to 90 minutes.
- Use a dedicated Slack channel: #game-day-YYYY-QX.
- Track timeline and actions in the game day doc; require at least one mitigation attempt per team.

Post-game-day report (within 7 days):
- What went well
- Observability gaps discovered
- Runbook updates required (link to PR)
- Action owner and ETA for remediation

Postmortem and RCA requirements
------------------------------
- Postmortem must be created for any Sev 1/Sev 2 incident with customer impact.
- Timeline: draft within 72 hours; final postmortem published within 14 days.
- Template fields (required):
  - Title
  - Incident ID
  - Date/time window
  - Summary (one paragraph)
  - Impact (customers affected, revenue impact if known)
  - Timeline (minute-level for first 2 hours, then high-level)
  - Root cause analysis
  - Mitigations during incident
  - Long-term fix and owners
  - Action items with owners and due dates
  - Metrics to validate fix
  - Lessons learned

Postmortem example header:
- Title: pm-2024-11-03-serving-tail-latency
- Owner: Maya R. Chen
- Publish: 2024-11-05

Status page and customer communication templates
------------------------------------------------
Status page conventions:
- Page: https://status.redwood.ai
- States: operational, degraded_performance, partial_outage, major_outage, maintenance
- Include a short impact blurb, affected regions/services, customer-visible ETA, and last_updated timestamp.

Customer-facing status template (short)
- Subject: Redwood API: Partial outage affecting text generation (Incident #ID)
- Body: Hello {CustomerName},
  We are investigating an issue impacting text generation for a subset of requests. Root cause appears to be {brief root cause}. Our mitigation is {brief mitigation}. Current ETA to resolution: {ETA_or_TBD}. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
  - Status page: https://status.redwood.ai
  - Support contact: support@redwood.ai

Internal status bulletin (for sales and CS)
- Subject: Internal: Incident {ID} — impact summary and customer list
- Body: Short summary, list of affected customers (if known), workaround guidance, expected customer questions and recommended responses. Attach meeting notes and postmortem link when available.

Communication cadence examples
- P0: Initial update within 10 minutes, follow-ups every 15 minutes.
- P1: Initial update within 30 minutes, follow-ups every 30–60 minutes.
- P2: Initial update within 4 hours, subsequent updates as resolution progresses.

Templates and automation snippets
-------------------------------
- Automated status API (example request):
  curl -X POST https://status-internal.redwood.ai/v1/incidents \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{"service":"redwood-serving","state":"partial_outage","short_summary":"High tail latency","started_at":"2025-01-10T14:03:00Z","update":"Working on mitigation"}'

- PagerDuty manual escalation (example):
  pd trigger --service redwood-serving-pd --summary "High tail latency affecting generation" --severity high

On-call playbook for managers (brief)
-----------------------------------
- Managers should avoid tactical mitigations unless asked; focus on removing blockers, ensuring escalations, and securing resources (additional engineers, exec comms).
- Managers must review all Sev 1 postmortems and confirm action items are scheduled in the team backlog within 7 days.

Governance and review cadence
---------------------------
- Runbooks: reviewed quarterly by owning team; last review date required on the runbook top.
- Rotation policy: reviewed annually; changes must be published and email-notified to oncall@redwood.ai.
- Game days: scheduled quarterly; executive summary sent to leadership after each cycle.

Appendices
---------
1) Incident doc template link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-doc-template
2) Runbook repository: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/ (authoritative runbooks live here)
3) Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
4) Escalation contact list (internal): /confluence/people-ops/escalation-contacts

Change log
----------
